summary.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover was Rs 239.49 crore (up 40.46% YoY) and value of production Rs 260.36 crore (up 7.9%). PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Defense about 66%, space (ISRO) about 21%, energy about 9%, others about 4%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Current-year export sales Rs 33 crore to date with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore; target about 10% of turnover (about Rs 100-120 crore).

segments.name: Titanium
segments.commentary: Melted about 750 tonnes last year after new melting facility; titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore cited. Management says titanium and super alloys carry higher margins than special steel.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 margins expected to be hit somewhat; management expects normalisation from Q3 FY27, with EBITDA margin returning toward 20-21%.
FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26 growth, though management said sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year is not practicable.
FY27 normal capex about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance; Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex over 2-3 years, with returns from year 4 and proposal still awaiting Board and ministry approval.
Metal bank: procurement under way for one customer; further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, with implementation targeted next quarter.
Aluminium JV plant at Nellore (with NALCO) being closed; a separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied 7000-series aluminium billets has been done as first commercial order.
Export expectation: at least 15-20% increase on the 10% export base over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex proposed for replacing ageing equipment; sent to ministry for evaluation, management declined to give timeline.
Isothermal forging completed in 6,000-tonne press for nickel-based super alloy for fighter aircraft engine; orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year.
New titanium melting facility commissioned last year; about 750 tonnes melted last year, with expected growth.
Spring plant in campus started; sample order received from BEML. Preliminary BAFA licence obtained for metal powder equipment, expected on campus by next year.
Bulletproof jacket (ABHED, from DRDO/IIT Delhi) fabricated; testing expected to complete this quarter, with test certificates by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Raw-material prices of nickel, molybdenum, tungsten rose sharply; cobalt also higher. Adverse price variance of about Rs 13 crore (or Rs 14 crore per later remark) in Q1.
LPG price nearly doubled due to Middle East conflict; furnaces are LPG-fired, affecting Q1 and possibly Q2.
Freight cost mostly booked at fixed terms; management said it sometimes absorbs freight increases on fixed-price contracts.
No nomination-based orders now; all orders won through competitive bidding.
Titanium sourced by import from Eastern Europe (former Russian Federation); management reports no import constraints currently.
Scrap usage in melt typically 50-60% for normal aerospace grades; virgin material mandated for human spaceflight and critical engine parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Madhubala Kalluri cited raw-material prices and LPG prices, which nearly doubled. She said Q2 may be hit, with normalisation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex takes 2-3 years, with returns from year 4. FY27 capex will be about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aluminium plant still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Nellore aluminium JV plant is being closed, pending ministry approval. The separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied aluminium billets is an alternative route.

qa_highlights.question: Will the S400 certification generate meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is testing-only revenue, conservatively estimated at about 10% of export base, with clarity in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to 20-21% in Q3 depends on LPG and raw-material prices easing; Q2 margin likely lower.
Fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed to raw-material and freight cost increases.
Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex is not yet Board- or ministry-approved; no timeline given.
Metal bank benefits are customer-owned and not on company balance sheet; implementation and utilisation are still to be confirmed.
Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and certifications, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, capex timelines and the scale of new orders. Management repeatedly attributed Q1 margin pressure to temporary LPG and raw-material factors and declined to quantify the Rs 1,000 crore capex return or the S400 revenue.

Only because of these little raw material and LPG issues only that was little lower bottom line.
So, we reduced our scrap inventory by Rs. 75 crores.
We are not going ahead with that plant.
